biggest_catch: NCP publishes no concrete earnings rate: official materials describe weekly points redeemable for catalog gift cards/prizes plus sweepstakes entries, but no points-to-dollar conversion is published anywhere, and membership itself is selective — you apply and NCP accepts only the demographics/areas it needs.
catches: No published points-to-dollar conversion: the value of a week's scanning is not stated in any official material.
Membership is selective and area-dependent — 'not everyone can join'; NCP recruits to match US population/demographic targets, and applicants may be waitlisted or rejected.

The concrete prizes NCP does publish are sweepstakes (chance-based): official sweepstakes rules show prizes like a $50 Amazon gift card; third parties cite $100 monthly / $500 quarterly / $5,000 cash-giveaway drawings.
Requires ongoing effort: scan every purchase's barcodes and transmit data weekly to keep earning.
Rewards are merchandise/gift cards from a catalog, not cash.

c1.evidence: National Consumer Panel is a real operating joint venture between Circana (formerly IRI) and NielsenIQ; official corporate site ncppanel.com describes recruitment via join.ncponline.com and the panel's data-collection business.

c2.evidence: No concrete payout terms published by the company: official materials describe points earned per week of participation redeemable for catalog gift cards/prizes and sweepstakes entries, but no points-to-dollar rate is published; the only concrete official prizes are chance-based sweepstakes (e.g., official NCP sweepstakes rules PDF: $50 Amazon gift card prizes).

c3.evidence: Joining is free; no participation fee in any official material.

c4.evidence: Official sources obtained: ncppanel.com (company/recruitment info) and the official NCP sweepstakes rules PDF on ncponline.com confirming real, company-run rewards.

eligibility: US consumers; recruited online via join.ncponline.com; selection is based on US population statistics and targeted demographic/geographic criteria — not everyone who applies is accepted.
notes: Rejected per the strict checklist: c2 fails. NCP is legitimate and operating (and members do receive gift cards per NCP's own blog), but the checklist requires concrete company-published payout terms and NCP publishes none — points have no stated dollar value and the published prizes are sweepstakes. Same rejection class as R0213 Nielsen. If NCP ever publishes a points schedule, this can be re-verified. Catalog headline '0' is directionally honest (no guaranteed $ amount), but the route stays unverified.

s1.note: Eligibility is selective: US only, demographic/geographic targeting, application required — confirmed on the official ncppanel.com page.

s2.note: No fee to join or participate.

s3.note: No official guaranteed payout timing — points accrue weekly; sweepstakes drawn on published schedules.

s4.note: Official materials make no guaranteed earnings claims, so there is nothing weasel-worded to flag; the absence of concrete figures is itself the c2 failure.

s5.note: https://www.ncppanel.com/the-power-of-national-consumer-panel/ — official NCP corporate domain, content returned by search tools.

s6.note: Participation steps are concrete (apply, scan barcodes weekly, transmit data), but the reward outcome has no concrete official value.

s7.note: Official NCP site and official sweepstakes rules PDF obtained via tool results 2026-09-22/23.

timing: No guaranteed payout schedule published; points accrue per week of participation; sweepstakes drawings run on published schedules.
